To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gradient expansion is the relativistic version of the drift approximation in the limit of low frequency and long wavelength, that it can be consistently implemented at any order and that it provides a natural framework to investigate the nonlinear evolution of curvature perturbations.

the gradient expansion and the drift approximation have a common large-scale limit, that they are physically complementary, and that the magnetized advection of the curvature perturbations, which is the dominant contribution to the evolution of the primordial magnetic fields in the nonlinear regime, is described by a nonlinear wave equation.

the gradient expansion is an alternative to the separate Universe paradigm for the analysis of the large-scale properties of the magnetized Universe, and that the magnetized advection equation for the curvature perturbation is a nonlinear equation, which, for a wide class of models, admits the same type of solutions as the linearized adiabat equation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description of magnetized plasmadynamics and its implications for the evolution of curvature perturbations.
a general relativistic description of magnetized fluids, where both the magnetic field and the spatial gradients of geometry and fluid variables are treated on the same footing.
the study of the properties of a magnetized fluid in the presence of spatial gradients, with particular emphasis on the evolution of the curvature perturbations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gradient expansion, as a perturbative expansion in gradients and in the relativistic in-homogeneities, provides a systematic and consistent description of the pre-decoupling magnetized plasma, which is complementary to the drift approximation, and which can be applied in the nonlinear regime.

the gradient expansion is the natural tool for the study of the magnetized plasma dynamics in the large-scale and low-frequency limit, and for the description of the evolution of the magnetically-induced curvature perturbations.

the gradient expansion is a useful tool for the investigation of the magnetized plas-ma physics in the presence of large-scale inhomogeneities, which is a crucial issue for a proper understanding of the generation of primordial magnetic fields in the early Universe and of the magnetohydro-dynamical evolution of the large-scale structures in the nonlinear regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gradient expansion of the magnetized plas-mas is a powerful and versatile tool for the investigation of the large-scale properties of the primordial Universe.
the magnetized plasma is a natural candidate to describe the physics of primordial magnetic fields in the early Universe.
the gradient expansion is an appropriate framework to study the evolution of curvature perturbations during the radiation era in the presence of large-scale magnetic fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the curvature perturbations are not affected by the magnetization, as long as the latter is sufficiently strong to be described in terms of the magnetic field.

, for the adiabatic modes, the curvature perturbations can be decomposed into a part that is conserved on super-Hubble scales and a part that is sourced by the spatial gradients of geometry and fluid.

the magnetized curvature fluctuations are sourced by the spatial gradients of both the fluid sources and the geometry, and that the former are the only source for the magnetized entropy perturbations.
